critical_code_review_comments: Fix is effective: separating scroll-follow into its own useEffect(deps=[input]) inside requestAnimationFrame with getScrollParent + direct scrollTop mutation and NO setState avoids the render-loop that previously triggered 'Maximum update depth exceeded'. Guarding setCaret against no-op writes further ensures state stability.

Observation: after ~400-450 chars the caret band locks at ~44% on desktop and ~42% on mobile — this is because the scroller has reached bottom (all lines visible) so no further scroll is needed. Confirmed via samples where top stays constant while typed count keeps increasing. This is correct behavior, not a bug.
Consider adding useLayoutEffect for setCaret to eliminate any tearing between paint and scroll, but functionally the current rAF flow is behaving correctly.

rca of the issue: Root cause of both prior bugs (iter_13) was that caret positioning useEffect performed BOTH setCaret (state write) AND scroller.scrollTop mutation in the same effect keyed on [input, chars]. The state write re-triggered the effect which computed a stale rect (React had not yet painted the new caret), so the delta was near-zero for repeat corrections, and setState-inside-effect combined with parent re-renders exceeded React's update depth. The fix (a) guards setCaret to only fire when left/top/height genuinely change, and (b) moves scroll-follow into a SEPARATE useEffect(deps=[input]) that runs inside requestAnimationFrame after paint, reads a fresh getBoundingClientRect, and performs a pure DOM mutation (scroller.scrollTop += delta) with NO setState. This breaks the feedback loop and lets the correction fire on every keystroke.
